title: Fleet Conservator: scaling simulator, operator playbook & timeline inspector
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a Fleet-level operator UI and backend simulator (the "Conservator") that lets SREs and capacity operators preview the downstream impact of scaling decisions, autoscaling policy changes, and throughput guarantees before applying them. The Conservator will replay historical traffic traces or run synthetic traffic to estimate latency/throughput/cost under different fleet configurations and provide a step-by-step operator playbook with rollback hooks and annotated change history.
problem_statement: Operators currently tune autoscaling policies and scaling knobs in production with limited visibility into how changes affect tail latency and token cost across tenants. This leads to cautious slow rollouts, surprise regressions, and manual incident-driven changes. We need a safe preview and action plan surface in the Console that reduces blast radius and shortens iteration time for fleet capacity changes.
scope: Console UX: new Conservator panel under Fleet Controls; timeline inspector that overlays past scaling events with simulated outcomes; scaling simulator backend service that consumes traces; operator playbook generator that emits step-by-step actions, SLO checks, and rollback recipes. Initial rollout supports Dedicated pools and host models; VPC/private will follow in subsequent cycle.
out_of_scope: Dedicated autoscaling agent (actual enforcement of policies in infra) and granular per-tenant cost allocation for first iteration.
acceptance_criteria: Conservator panel accessible from Fleet Controls with a simulator entry point
Ability to ingest a 48-hour traffic trace and run a deterministic simulation showing throughput, 95/99 latency, and estimated token cost for candidate scaling changes
Simulator UI shows side-by-side baseline vs candidate path with visual diff on latency and cost
Operator playbook generated with: recommended safe step size, cooldown windows, canary percentage, health checks to monitor, and rollback steps
Change history inspector lists prior scaling decisions with annotations and links to related PRs/incident notes
Backend API endpoints and job scheduling for simulation run are instrumented and surfaced in Console telemetry
Tests: synthetic scenario suite (cold-start surge, slow-degrade, long-tail growth) included in CI; UX smoke tests for the new panel
notes: Engineering spike validated that replaying 48h traces provides stable estimates within ±8% for 95p latency using current runtime kernels
Trade-off: limit replay window to 48h for speed and noise reduction; longer windows increase compute cost and produce less actionable short-term guidance
Decision: simulation uses sampled KV-cache behavior model rather than full KV cache emulation to keep runtime in <10min for 48h traces
Risk: synthetic replay may under-represent multi-tenant interference; mitigation: flag confidence level and add a conservative multiplier to recommendations
Cost model: use token-rate * avg-cost-per-token per model variant and add burst buffer pricing as configurable parameter
UX: slider-based 'step-simulate' to preview incremental scale-ups, plus a timeline scrubber to inspect historical events and their simulated alternative outcomes

2026-02-24: ENG spike complete — prototype replay service (trace -> simulator) produced 3 scenarios and baseline comparison. Prototype results shared with Product and Design.
2026-03-02: Design critique — added timeline scrubber and confidence band overlay. Decided to surface conservative multiplier for low-confidence simulations.
2026-03-05: Backend API contract drafted: POST /api/v1/fleet/simulate {trace_id, candidate_change, window_hours} -> job_id; GET /api/v1/fleet/simulate/job/{job_id} -> results
2026-03-08: QA plan written; synthetic scenario suite added. Found an edge case where cold-start simulation underestimates tail for model variants with large KV footprints — flagged as follow-up.
2026-03-10: UX copy and accessibility pass complete. Handed off to Eng for review PR. Preparing demo for Capacity Guild on 2026-03-16.
Next: finalize rollout gating, add telemetry hooks for confidence scoring, schedule canary with one customer beta
open_questions: Should playbook recommend model-variant-specific scaling or fleet-wide knobs only for v1?
What CI guardrails do we need to prevent accidental 'apply' of simulation results without manual approval?
How do we show confidence to non-engineering operators (simple color band vs numeric%)?
implementation_notes: Backend: reuse trace ingestion pipeline from evals-service; add simulator worker pool separate from serving runtime to avoid contention
Data retention: store trace samples and simulation results for 30 days; provide export to S3 for longer-term audits
Frontend: new Conservator React route under /fleet/:id/conservator; components: TimelineInspector, SimulatorControls, PlaybookPanel, ChangeHistoryDiff
Telemetry: emit simulation.confidence, simulation.duration_ms, and predicted_95p_delta to console-telemetry
APIs: simulate job must validate candidate_change against guardrails (max_scale_per_min, max_total_instances) before enqueuing
